section_title: About FleetHarbor Logistics
content: FleetHarbor Logistics is a third-party logistics (3PL) provider offering warehousing, freight booking, last-mile delivery and shipment tracking for manufacturers and retail clients in western India. Operations run from three distribution warehouses in Ahmedabad, Vadodara and Rajkot.

section_title: Service levels
content: Standard delivery windows are 2 to 4 business days for intra-state shipments and 4 to 7 business days for inter-state shipments. Priority shipments are flagged at booking and receive daily status checks from the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Order lifecycle
content: Every order moves through six stages: Order Created, Order Confirmed, Picked, Packed, Dispatched and Delivered. An exception at any stage is logged as a hold with a reason code and does not cancel the order.

section_title: Roles in the workflow
content: Clients place orders through the client portal or API. Logistics Coordinators validate and book shipments, Warehouse Managers oversee picking, packing and dispatch, and Delivery Executives complete last-mile delivery and proof of delivery.

section_title: Shipment booking
content: A Logistics Coordinator books each confirmed order within 2 hours. A booking needs the pickup address, consignee address, weight, dimensions, number of cartons and declared value. The LR number is generated at booking.

section_title: Carrier selection
content: Carriers are chosen by lane rate, service level and available capacity, with preferred carriers used first. Hazardous goods can only move with a carrier holding a valid hazmat certificate.

section_title: Shipping documents
content: Every dispatch needs an invoice and a packing list. An e-way bill is required for consignments valued above INR 50,000, as per applicable GST rules. Dispatch is blocked in the system until the mandatory documents are attached.

section_title: Receiving inbound goods
content: Inbound goods are checked against the Advance Shipping Notice (ASN). Any unit discrepancy above 2 percent must be reported to the Warehouse Manager within 4 hours of receipt, with photos and the ASN reference.

section_title: Storage zones
content: Fast-moving SKUs are stored in Zone A near the dispatch bays. Hazardous items are stored only in Zone H. Every bin location is recorded in the Warehouse Management System (WMS) at put-away.

section_title: Picking and packing
content: Perishable SKUs are picked using FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) and all other SKUs using FIFO (First In, First Out). Every carton is weighed and labelled before it leaves the packing station.

section_title: How to track an order
content: Customers can track a shipment with their order ID or LR number on the client portal, or by calling support. In-transit shipments refresh every 30 minutes.

section_title: Tracking identifiers
content: Order IDs begin with ORD- and LR numbers begin with LR-. After booking, use the LR number to track, because it is the identifier shared with the carrier.

section_title: Delivery attempts
content: A Delivery Executive can make up to three delivery attempts. Each failed attempt is recorded with a reason code. After the third failed attempt, the shipment returns to the origin hub.

section_title: Proof of delivery
content: Proof of delivery (POD) must include the receiver's name, a signature or OTP confirmation, and a timestamp. Photos are mandatory for fragile goods.

section_title: Delivery hours
content: Deliveries run between 9:00 AM and 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Deliveries outside these hours need written approval from the Operations Manager and the client.

section_title: Where is my order?
content: Check the tracking page with your order ID. If the status has not changed in 24 hours, contact the Logistics Coordinator for your lane.

section_title: Changing the delivery address
content: Address changes are accepted only before dispatch. After dispatch, a change must be requested through the carrier and may attract a re-routing fee.

section_title: Damaged goods on arrival
content: Note the damage on the POD at delivery, then raise a claim within 7 days with photos and the invoice. See PO-001 for liability limits.

section_title: Same-day dispatch cutoff
content: Orders confirmed by 1:00 PM are dispatched the same day from the originating warehouse. Later orders are dispatched the next working day.

section_title: Damage and claims policy
content: Claims must be filed within 7 days of delivery. Carrier liability is limited to the declared value of the goods unless extended cover was purchased at booking.

section_title: Returns policy
content: Returns are accepted within 10 days of delivery for unused goods in original packaging. Return freight is charged to the client unless the return results from a FleetHarbor error.

section_title: Data and privacy
content: Consignee contact details are used only for delivery and are removed from active systems 90 days after proof of delivery. Consignee personal data must not be shared with third parties.

section_title: Escalation matrix
content: Level 1 is the Logistics Coordinator, Level 2 the Operations Manager and Level 3 the Head of Operations. Escalate a priority shipment to the next level if it has no resolution within 4 hours.

section_title: Status: Booked
content: The shipment has an LR number and an assigned carrier but has not yet been picked up.

section_title: Status: In Transit
content: The carrier has picked up the shipment and it is moving between hubs.

section_title: Status: Out for Delivery
content: The shipment has reached the destination hub or is with the Delivery Executive for delivery today.

section_title: Status: Delayed / On Hold
content: The shipment is delayed because of weather, missing documents or capacity limits. The reason code is shown on the tracking page.

section_title: Status: Delivered, Failed Attempt, Returned
content: Delivered means POD is captured. Failed Attempt means a delivery was tried but not completed. Returned means the shipment is on its way back to origin.

section_title: LR (Lorry Receipt)
content: A transport document issued by the carrier as proof that goods have been booked for transport. It carries the LR number used for tracking.

section_title: FEFO and FIFO
content: FEFO means First Expiry, First Out and FIFO means First In, First Out. These are the two picking methods used in the warehouse.

section_title: ASN and POD
content: An Advance Shipping Notice (ASN) is sent by the supplier before goods arrive. Proof of Delivery (POD) is the signed record that goods reached the consignee.

section_title: 3PL, LTL and FTL
content: 3PL is third-party logistics. LTL (less-than-truckload) is a shared truck for smaller loads, and FTL (full-truckload) is a truck dedicated to one shipment.

section_title: Ahmedabad to Vadodara: delivery window
content: Shipments from Ahmedabad to Vadodara (Gujarat) are an intra-state movement within Gujarat. The standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days, as set out in the service levels. Priority shipments on this lane are flagged at booking and get daily status checks from the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Ahmedabad to Vadodara: booking and dispatch cutoff
content: A Logistics Coordinator books each Ahmedabad to Vadodara order within 2 hours of confirmation. Orders confirmed by 1:00 PM are dispatched the same day from Ahmedabad, and later orders are dispatched on the next working day.

section_title: Ahmedabad to Vadodara: documents needed
content: A Ahmedabad to Vadodara dispatch needs a commercial invoice, a packing list and the LR number generated at booking. Consignments valued above INR 50,000 also need an e-way bill under GST rules. Because this movement stays within Gujarat, the consignee address on the invoice must match the delivery address. Dispatch stays blocked until the mandatory documents are attached.

section_title: Ahmedabad to Vadodara: delivery and proof of delivery
content: Shipments from Ahmedabad to Vadodara are delivered in Vadodara between 9:00 AM and 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Up to three delivery attempts are made, and each failed attempt is logged with a reason code. The proof of delivery must show the receiver's name, a signature or OTP confirmation and a timestamp.

section_title: Ahmedabad to Vadodara: delays and escalation
content: If a Ahmedabad to Vadodara shipment is delayed or on hold, the tracking page shows a reason code such as weather, missing documents or capacity limits. A priority shipment moves to the next escalation level if it has no resolution within 4 hours.

section_title: Sending electronic goods from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Keep units in their original boxes with anti-static packing, and never stack heavy cartons on electronics. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. For a damage claim, photograph the carton and the unit, and keep the serial number from the invoice.

section_title: Sending garments from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Pack in polybags with a moisture barrier, and keep cartons away from chemicals and food. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. Count pieces against the packing list at delivery and write any shortage on the POD.

section_title: Sending ambient pharmaceuticals from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Keep batch numbers visible on every carton, store away from direct sunlight and heat, and send the batch certificate with the invoice. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. Record batch and expiry details on the POD, and report any broken tamper seal before signing.

section_title: Sending perishable food from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Pick perishables FEFO, and confirm any temperature requirement at booking before dispatch. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. If product is spoiled, note the condition on the POD, and raise a claim with photos and the invoice within 7 days.

section_title: Sending packaged FMCG goods from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Stack cartons by SKU with labels facing out, respect the stacking limit printed on each carton, and check expiry dates at receiving. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. Note any crushed or wet cartons on the POD and keep them until the claim is closed.

section_title: Sending auto and machinery parts from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Secure heavy parts with straps or blocking so they do not shift, and mark the weight on each carton. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. Check for shifted or cracked parts at delivery, and record the part numbers on the POD.

section_title: Sending ceramic tiles and glassware from Ahmedabad to Vadodara
content: Use edge protectors and partition cartons, mark cartons FRAGILE on all sides, and load them upright where possible. This Ahmedabad to Vadodara lane is intra-state, so the standard delivery window is 2 to 4 business days from dispatch. Photos are mandatory for fragile goods at delivery (see DP-002), so take them before signing.

section_title: Commercial invoice: what it is
content: The seller's bill to the buyer, showing the goods, quantities, unit prices and total value. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Commercial invoice: when it is required
content: Needed for almost every dispatch, both domestic and export, and used to declare the value. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Commercial invoice: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the consignee name, HSN code, quantities and value match the packing list. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Packing list: what it is
content: A document listing each carton's contents, weight and dimensions. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Packing list: when it is required
content: Required with every dispatch so the consignee can verify what arrived. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Packing list: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the carton count and total weight match the physical cartons. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: E-way bill: what it is
content: A GST document, identified by a 12-digit number, that tracks goods moving by road. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: E-way bill: when it is required
content: Required for consignments valued above INR 50,000 under GST rules. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: E-way bill: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the e-way bill is valid for the route and that the vehicle number is correct. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Delivery challan: what it is
content: A GST document issued when goods move without a sale, such as for job work or a branch transfer. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Delivery challan: when it is required
content: Needed when stock moves between locations or goes out for processing. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Delivery challan: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the challan lists the goods, quantities and purpose of movement. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Tax invoice: when it is required

section_title: Tax invoice: checks before dispatch

section_title: Bill of lading: when it is required

section_title: Bill of lading: checks before dispatch

content: A document proving that the goods are insured for transit. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Insurance certificate: when it is required
content: Needed when extended cover is bought at booking (see PO-001). If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Insurance certificate: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the insured value and policy period cover the shipment. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Safety data sheet (SDS): what it is
content: A document that describes a chemical's hazards, handling, storage and emergency measures. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Safety data sheet (SDS): when it is required
content: Required for chemicals and dangerous goods. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Safety data sheet (SDS): checks before dispatch
content: Check that the SDS matches the product and is attached to the dispatch. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Certificate of analysis (CoA): what it is
content: A quality certificate that shows the test results for a batch. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Certificate of analysis (CoA): when it is required
content: Needed when a buyer asks for proof of batch quality, which is common for pharmaceuticals and chemicals. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Certificate of analysis (CoA): checks before dispatch
content: Check that the batch number on the CoA matches the cartons. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Batch certificate: what it is
content: A document confirming that a batch was released by the manufacturer. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Batch certificate: when it is required
content: Needed for pharmaceutical shipments. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Batch certificate: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the batch numbers on the certificate match the cartons. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Mill test certificate: what it is
content: A certificate from the steel mill showing the material grade and test results. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Mill test certificate: when it is required
content: Needed for steel shipments when the buyer asks for it. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Mill test certificate: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the heat numbers on the certificate match the bundles. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Fumigation certificate: what it is
content: A certificate confirming that goods were treated against pests. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Fumigation certificate: when it is required
content: Needed when the destination or client requires pest-free proof, which is common for food grains. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Fumigation certificate: checks before dispatch
content: Check the treatment date and method on the certificate. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Phytosanitary certificate: what it is
content: A plant health certificate confirming that plant produce is free of listed pests. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Phytosanitary certificate: when it is required
content: Needed for some plant and produce exports where the destination requires it. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Phytosanitary certificate: checks before dispatch
content: Check the issuing authority and the consignment details. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Warranty card: what it is
content: A card that shows the product's warranty terms and proof of purchase. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Warranty card: when it is required
content: Included with electronics and appliances when the manufacturer supplies it. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Warranty card: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the serial number on the card matches the carton. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Goods receipt note (GRN): what it is
content: A warehouse record confirming that goods were received and checked. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Goods receipt note (GRN): when it is required
content: Created at receiving for every inbound consignment. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Goods receipt note (GRN): checks before dispatch
content: Check that the received quantities and any discrepancy are recorded. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Pro forma invoice: what it is
content: A preliminary invoice sent before the final invoice, often to agree terms or arrange payment. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Pro forma invoice: when it is required
content: Used before an export order is confirmed. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Pro forma invoice: checks before dispatch
content: Check that it is marked pro forma and is replaced by the commercial invoice at dispatch. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Dock receipt: what it is
content: A receipt issued by a port or container terminal when a container is accepted. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Dock receipt: when it is required
content: Used for container shipments handed over at a terminal. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Dock receipt: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the container number and seal number match the booking. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Gate pass: what it is
content: A pass that allows a vehicle or person to enter or leave a site. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Gate pass: when it is required
content: Used at warehouse and port gates. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Gate pass: checks before dispatch
content: Check the vehicle number and the date on the pass. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Weighment slip: what it is
content: A slip showing the weight of a loaded vehicle, recorded at a weighbridge. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Weighment slip: when it is required
content: Needed when a load weight must be confirmed for billing or compliance. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Weighment slip: checks before dispatch
content: Check the vehicle number and the gross and tare weights. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Dangerous goods declaration: what it is
content: A signed declaration that a consignment is correctly classified, packed and labelled as dangerous goods. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Dangerous goods declaration: when it is required
content: Required for every dangerous goods shipment. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Dangerous goods declaration: checks before dispatch
content: Check the UN number, hazard class and packing group. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: ISPM 15 wood packaging mark: what it is
content: A stamp showing that wooden packaging was heat-treated or fumigated to international standards. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: ISPM 15 wood packaging mark: when it is required
content: Needed for export shipments that use wooden pallets or crates. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: ISPM 15 wood packaging mark: checks before dispatch
content: Check that the stamp is visible on the wood. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Quality inspection report: what it is
content: A report from an inspection of goods before shipment. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Quality inspection report: when it is required
content: Requested by the buyer or client for high-value or regulated goods. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Quality inspection report: checks before dispatch
content: Check the inspection date and the lot or batch covered. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Authorisation letter: what it is
content: A letter that authorises a person or company to collect or clear goods. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Authorisation letter: when it is required
content: Needed when someone other than the consignee collects the goods. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Authorisation letter: checks before dispatch
content: Check the signatory and the validity date. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Delivery order: what it is
content: A document that authorises release of goods from a warehouse, port or terminal. The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Delivery order: when it is required
content: Used when goods leave a warehouse or terminal under a release order. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Delivery order: checks before dispatch
content: Check the order number, consignee and quantities. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Proof of delivery (POD): what it is
content: The signed record that goods reached the consignee (see TM-003). The document travels with the consignment file, so it is kept with the invoice and packing list until the shipment is delivered.

section_title: Proof of delivery (POD): when it is required
content: Required for every completed delivery. If a required copy is missing, tell the Logistics Coordinator before dispatch so the shipment is not put on hold (see SS-004).

section_title: Proof of delivery (POD): checks before dispatch
content: Check that the receiver's name, signature or OTP and timestamp are captured. Record any mismatch in the booking notes and inform the Logistics Coordinator before the vehicle leaves.

section_title: Tracking event: Booking Confirmed
content: The shipment is booked and an LR number is generated for tracking. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Booking Confirmed: what to do
content: The shipment is booked and an LR number is generated for tracking. What to do: Keep the LR number, because the carrier uses it too.

section_title: Booking Confirmed: what happens next
content: The shipment is booked and an LR number is generated for tracking. What happens next: A pickup is scheduled with the assigned carrier.

section_title: Tracking event: Pickup Scheduled
content: A carrier has been assigned to collect the goods on a set day. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Pickup Scheduled: what to do
content: A carrier has been assigned to collect the goods on a set day. What to do: Make sure someone at the pickup address can hand over the goods.

section_title: Pickup Scheduled: what happens next
content: A carrier has been assigned to collect the goods on a set day. What happens next: The carrier collects the goods and the status changes.

section_title: Tracking event: Pickup Attempted
content: The carrier reached the pickup address but could not collect the goods. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Pickup Attempted: what to do
content: The carrier reached the pickup address but could not collect the goods. What to do: Check that the goods are ready and that the contact person is reachable.

section_title: Pickup Attempted: what happens next
content: The carrier reached the pickup address but could not collect the goods. What happens next: A new pickup is scheduled.

section_title: Tracking event: Picked Up
content: The carrier has collected the goods from the shipper. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Picked Up: what to do
content: The carrier has collected the goods from the shipper. What to do: No action is needed unless the carton count is wrong.

section_title: Picked Up: what happens next
content: The carrier has collected the goods from the shipper. What happens next: The goods move to the origin hub.

section_title: Tracking event: Received at Origin Hub
content: The goods reached the origin warehouse and are being checked in. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Received at Origin Hub: what to do
content: The goods reached the origin warehouse and are being checked in. What to do: Nothing is needed. You can check the tracking page at any time.

section_title: Received at Origin Hub: what happens next
content: The goods reached the origin warehouse and are being checked in. What happens next: The goods are packed, sealed and labelled.

section_title: Tracking event: Packed and Sealed
content: The cartons are packed, weighed and labelled at the packing station. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Packed and Sealed: what to do
content: The cartons are packed, weighed and labelled at the packing station. What to do: No action is needed.

section_title: Packed and Sealed: what happens next
content: The cartons are packed, weighed and labelled at the packing station. What happens next: The cartons are loaded onto the vehicle.

section_title: Tracking event: Loaded on Vehicle
content: The cartons are loaded and the vehicle number is recorded. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Loaded on Vehicle: what to do
content: The cartons are loaded and the vehicle number is recorded. What to do: Keep the vehicle number for reference.

section_title: Loaded on Vehicle: what happens next
content: The cartons are loaded and the vehicle number is recorded. What happens next: The vehicle departs the origin hub.

section_title: Tracking event: Departed Origin Hub
content: The vehicle has left the origin warehouse. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Departed Origin Hub: what to do
content: The vehicle has left the origin warehouse. What to do: Track the LR number for the next update.

section_title: Departed Origin Hub: what happens next
content: The vehicle has left the origin warehouse. What happens next: The shipment moves in transit to the next hub.

section_title: Tracking event: In Transit
content: The shipment is moving between hubs (see SS-002). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: In Transit: what to do
content: The shipment is moving between hubs (see SS-002). What to do: Wait for the next update. In-transit status refreshes every 30 minutes.

section_title: In Transit: what happens next
content: The shipment is moving between hubs (see SS-002). What happens next: The shipment reaches a transit hub or the destination hub.

section_title: Tracking event: Arrived at Transit Hub
content: The shipment reached an intermediate hub on its route. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Arrived at Transit Hub: what to do
content: The shipment reached an intermediate hub on its route. What to do: No action is needed.

section_title: Arrived at Transit Hub: what happens next
content: The shipment reached an intermediate hub on its route. What happens next: It departs for the next leg of the route.

section_title: Tracking event: Arrived at Destination Hub
content: The shipment reached the hub that serves the delivery city. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Arrived at Destination Hub: what to do
content: The shipment reached the hub that serves the delivery city. What to do: Check whether a delivery is already scheduled.

section_title: Arrived at Destination Hub: what happens next
content: The shipment reached the hub that serves the delivery city. What happens next: The goods are unloaded and sorted for delivery.

section_title: Tracking event: Unloaded and Sorted
content: The cartons are unloaded and sorted by delivery route. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Unloaded and Sorted: what to do
content: The cartons are unloaded and sorted by delivery route. What to do: No action is needed.

section_title: Unloaded and Sorted: what happens next
content: The cartons are unloaded and sorted by delivery route. What happens next: The shipment is assigned to a Delivery Executive.

section_title: Tracking event: Out for Delivery
content: A Delivery Executive is taking the shipment to the consignee today (see SS-003). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Out for Delivery: what to do
content: A Delivery Executive is taking the shipment to the consignee today (see SS-003). What to do: Make sure the receiver is available to sign.

section_title: Out for Delivery: what happens next
content: A Delivery Executive is taking the shipment to the consignee today (see SS-003). What happens next: A delivery attempt is made within delivery hours.

section_title: Tracking event: Delivery Attempted
content: A delivery was tried but could not be completed. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Delivery Attempted: what to do
content: A delivery was tried but could not be completed. What to do: Contact the Logistics Coordinator if the address or time is wrong.

section_title: Delivery Attempted: what happens next
content: A delivery was tried but could not be completed. What happens next: Another attempt is made, up to three attempts in total.

section_title: Tracking event: Delivered
content: The consignee received the goods and the POD is captured (see SS-005). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Delivered: what to do
content: The consignee received the goods and the POD is captured (see SS-005). What to do: Check the goods and write any damage or shortage on the POD.

section_title: Delivered: what happens next
content: The consignee received the goods and the POD is captured (see SS-005). What happens next: Nothing further. The shipment is complete.

section_title: Tracking event: POD Uploaded
content: The signed proof of delivery has been uploaded to the system. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: POD Uploaded: what to do
content: The signed proof of delivery has been uploaded to the system. What to do: Download the POD from the client portal if you need a copy.

section_title: POD Uploaded: what happens next
content: The signed proof of delivery has been uploaded to the system. What happens next: The shipment record is closed.

section_title: Tracking event: Consignee Unavailable
content: Nobody was present at the delivery address during the attempt. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Consignee Unavailable: what to do
content: Nobody was present at the delivery address during the attempt. What to do: Tell the Logistics Coordinator the best time for the next attempt.

section_title: Consignee Unavailable: what happens next
content: Nobody was present at the delivery address during the attempt. What happens next: The next attempt is scheduled within delivery hours.

section_title: Tracking event: Address Not Found
content: The delivery address could not be located. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Address Not Found: what to do
content: The delivery address could not be located. What to do: Send a corrected address or a nearby landmark to the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Address Not Found: what happens next
content: The delivery address could not be located. What happens next: The address is verified before the next attempt.

section_title: Tracking event: Refused by Consignee
content: The consignee refused the delivery. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Refused by Consignee: what to do
content: The consignee refused the delivery. What to do: Contact the Logistics Coordinator to agree the next step with the sender.

section_title: Refused by Consignee: what happens next
content: The consignee refused the delivery. What happens next: The shipment is re-attempted or returned as agreed.

section_title: Tracking event: Rescheduled
content: The delivery date was moved at the request of the sender or receiver. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Rescheduled: what to do
content: The delivery date was moved at the request of the sender or receiver. What to do: Confirm the new date with your Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Rescheduled: what happens next
content: The delivery date was moved at the request of the sender or receiver. What happens next: Delivery happens on the new date.

section_title: Tracking event: Held for Documents
content: Required documents are missing, so the shipment is on hold (see SS-004). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Held for Documents: what to do
content: Required documents are missing, so the shipment is on hold (see SS-004). What to do: Send the missing invoice or e-way bill to the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Held for Documents: what happens next
content: Required documents are missing, so the shipment is on hold (see SS-004). What happens next: The hold is released once the documents are attached.

section_title: Tracking event: Held for Weather
content: Weather is delaying road movement. The reason code is shown on the tracking page. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Held for Weather: what to do
content: Weather is delaying road movement. The reason code is shown on the tracking page. What to do: Expect a delay. No action is needed.

section_title: Held for Weather: what happens next
content: Weather is delaying road movement. The reason code is shown on the tracking page. What happens next: Movement resumes when conditions improve.

section_title: Tracking event: Held for Road Block
content: A road closure or traffic restriction is delaying the vehicle. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Held for Road Block: what to do
content: A road closure or traffic restriction is delaying the vehicle. What to do: No action is needed. Monitor the status.

section_title: Held for Road Block: what happens next
content: A road closure or traffic restriction is delaying the vehicle. What happens next: The vehicle is re-routed or resumes its route.

section_title: Tracking event: Vehicle Breakdown
content: The vehicle developed a fault on the way. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Vehicle Breakdown: what to do
content: The vehicle developed a fault on the way. What to do: Expect a delay. The Logistics Coordinator may arrange a replacement vehicle.

section_title: Vehicle Breakdown: what happens next
content: The vehicle developed a fault on the way. What happens next: The goods transfer to a replacement vehicle.

section_title: Tracking event: Capacity Shortage
content: The carrier does not have enough capacity to move the shipment on the planned date. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Capacity Shortage: what to do
content: The carrier does not have enough capacity to move the shipment on the planned date. What to do: Ask the Logistics Coordinator for the revised date.

section_title: Capacity Shortage: what happens next
content: The carrier does not have enough capacity to move the shipment on the planned date. What happens next: A different vehicle is assigned.

section_title: Tracking event: Damage Reported in Transit
content: Damage was noted at a hub or during transit. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Damage Reported in Transit: what to do
content: Damage was noted at a hub or during transit. What to do: Keep the packaging and take photos at delivery.

section_title: Damage Reported in Transit: what happens next
content: Damage was noted at a hub or during transit. What happens next: A damage claim is opened under PO-001.

section_title: Tracking event: Shortage Reported
content: A count at a hub shows fewer cartons than the packing list. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Shortage Reported: what to do
content: A count at a hub shows fewer cartons than the packing list. What to do: Compare the invoice and packing list with the cartons you received.

section_title: Shortage Reported: what happens next
content: A count at a hub shows fewer cartons than the packing list. What happens next: The discrepancy is investigated.

section_title: Tracking event: Hold Released
content: The reason for the hold has been cleared. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Hold Released: what to do
content: The reason for the hold has been cleared. What to do: No action is needed.

section_title: Hold Released: what happens next
content: The reason for the hold has been cleared. What happens next: The shipment resumes its route.

section_title: Tracking event: Re-routed
content: The shipment is sent by a different route to avoid a delay. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Re-routed: what to do
content: The shipment is sent by a different route to avoid a delay. What to do: Expect a changed transit time.

section_title: Re-routed: what happens next
content: The shipment is sent by a different route to avoid a delay. What happens next: The shipment continues to the destination.

section_title: Tracking event: Return Initiated
content: The shipment has been marked for return to the origin (see DP-001). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Return Initiated: what to do
content: The shipment has been marked for return to the origin (see DP-001). What to do: Confirm with the sender what to do with the goods.

section_title: Return Initiated: what happens next
content: The shipment has been marked for return to the origin (see DP-001). What happens next: The return leg is dispatched.

section_title: Tracking event: Returned to Origin
content: The shipment has reached the origin hub after a return. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Returned to Origin: what to do
content: The shipment has reached the origin hub after a return. What to do: Arrange the next step with the sender.

section_title: Returned to Origin: what happens next
content: The shipment has reached the origin hub after a return. What happens next: The goods are received back into stock.

section_title: Tracking event: Cancelled
content: The booking was cancelled before the goods were picked up. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Cancelled: what to do
content: The booking was cancelled before the goods were picked up. What to do: Confirm the cancellation in writing if you need a record.

section_title: Cancelled: what happens next
content: The booking was cancelled before the goods were picked up. What happens next: The LR is closed.

section_title: Tracking event: Address Change Requested
content: A change of delivery address was requested (see FAQ-002). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Address Change Requested: what to do
content: A change of delivery address was requested (see FAQ-002). What to do: Confirm the new address and any re-routing fee.

section_title: Address Change Requested: what happens next
content: A change of delivery address was requested (see FAQ-002). What happens next: The change is applied if the shipment can still be re-routed.

section_title: Tracking event: Priority Flag Added
content: The shipment was marked priority at booking or later (see CO-002). This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Priority Flag Added: what to do
content: The shipment was marked priority at booking or later (see CO-002). What to do: Expect daily status checks from the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Priority Flag Added: what happens next
content: The shipment was marked priority at booking or later (see CO-002). What happens next: Escalation applies if there is no resolution within 4 hours.

section_title: Tracking event: Documents Verified
content: The required documents were checked and accepted. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Documents Verified: what to do
content: The required documents were checked and accepted. What to do: No action is needed.

section_title: Documents Verified: what happens next
content: The required documents were checked and accepted. What happens next: Dispatch continues.

section_title: Tracking event: Returned Delivered
content: The returned shipment reached the sender. This event is shown on the tracking page for the shipment.

section_title: Returned Delivered: what to do
content: The returned shipment reached the sender. What to do: Confirm receipt with the Logistics Coordinator.

section_title: Returned Delivered: what happens next
content: The returned shipment reached the sender. What happens next: The shipment record is closed.

section_title: Bill of lading (B/L)
content: A sea freight document issued by the ocean carrier. It is evidence that cargo was received and of the terms of the shipping contract.

section_title: Airway bill (AWB)
content: The air cargo document issued by the airline or forwarder for a consignment. Unlike a bill of lading, it is not a title document.

section_title: Bin
content: A numbered storage location in the warehouse, recorded in the WMS.

section_title: Bulk cargo
content: Goods shipped loose rather than in packages, such as grain or coal.

section_title: Carrier
content: The company that physically moves the goods, such as a road transporter, airline or shipping line.

section_title: Carton
content: A corrugated cardboard box used as the basic outer pack for a shipment.

section_title: Chargeable weight
content: The higher of actual weight and volumetric weight, used to price a shipment.

section_title: Consignee
content: The person or company who receives the goods.

section_title: Consignor
content: The person or company who sends the goods. Also called the shipper.

section_title: Container
content: A standard steel box used for sea and rail freight, usually 20 or 40 feet long.

section_title: Cross-docking
content: Moving goods straight from inbound to outbound with little or no storage in between.

section_title: Customs broker
content: A licensed agent who files customs declarations for an importer or exporter.

section_title: Cycle count
content: A partial stock count done on a rolling schedule, instead of one full stock take.

section_title: Dead stock
content: Inventory that has not moved for a long time and is unlikely to sell.

section_title: Demurrage
content: A charge for leaving a container at a port or terminal beyond the free time.

section_title: Detention
content: A charge for keeping a container outside the terminal beyond the free time.

section_title: Dimensional weight
content: Another name for volumetric weight, calculated from the length, width and height of a shipment.

section_title: Dispatch
content: Sending a shipment out of the warehouse together with its documents.

section_title: Dunnage
content: Packing material, such as wood or inflatable bags, that stops cargo moving inside a container or vehicle.

section_title: Incoterms
content: Standard international trade terms that set who pays for transport and who carries the risk at each stage of a sale.

section_title: EXW (Ex Works)
content: The buyer collects the goods from the seller's premises and takes on most of the cost and risk.

section_title: FOB (Free on Board)
content: The seller delivers the goods on board the vessel at the port of shipment.

section_title: CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight)
content: The seller pays the cost, insurance and freight to the named destination port.

section_title: DAP (Delivered at Place)
content: The seller delivers the goods ready for unloading at the named place. The buyer handles import clearance.

section_title: DDP (Delivered Duty Paid)
content: The seller delivers the goods cleared for import, with all duties paid.

section_title: Forwarder
content: A company that arranges transport and paperwork for shipments, often using several carriers.

section_title: Freight
content: The charge for moving goods, or the goods being moved, depending on the context.

section_title: Goods receipt note (GRN)
content: A record made at receiving that confirms goods arrived and were checked.

section_title: GST (Goods and Services Tax)
content: India's indirect tax on the supply of goods and services.

section_title: GSTIN
content: The 15-character GST identification number of a registered business.

section_title: HSN code
content: A standard code that classifies goods for GST purposes.

section_title: HS code
content: The Harmonized System code used internationally to classify goods for customs duty.

section_title: Hub
content: A consolidation or distribution point where shipments are sorted and transferred.

section_title: ICD (Inland Container Depot)
content: A container terminal located inland, where containers are stored, cleared and transferred.

section_title: Inbound
content: Goods coming into a warehouse or location.

section_title: Inventory
content: The stock of goods a business holds.

section_title: Last mile
content: The final leg of delivery, from a local hub to the consignee.

section_title: Load securing
content: Methods such as straps, blocking and bracing that stop cargo moving during transit.

section_title: Lot number
content: A code that groups items made or received together, used for traceability.

section_title: Manifest
content: A list of all the shipments or items on one vehicle, flight or vessel.

section_title: Mode of transport
content: The method used to move goods, such as road, rail, air, sea or a combination.

section_title: Outbound
content: Goods leaving a warehouse or location.

section_title: Pallet
content: A flat platform, usually wood or plastic, used to move and stack goods with a forklift.

section_title: Pick list
content: The list of items and bin locations a picker follows to gather an order.

section_title: Put-away
content: Moving received goods into their storage bins and recording the location.

section_title: Quarantine
content: A separate area for goods on hold, such as damaged or unverified stock.

section_title: Reason code
content: A short code that explains why a shipment has an exception, such as a hold or delay.

section_title: Reverse logistics
content: Moving goods back from the consignee for return, repair or disposal.

section_title: Route
content: The planned sequence of hubs and legs that a shipment follows.

section_title: Safety stock
content: Extra stock kept to cover unexpected demand or late supply.

section_title: SKU (stock keeping unit)
content: A unique code for each distinct product variant held in stock.

section_title: Shrinkage
content: Stock lost from inventory through damage, theft or counting errors.

section_title: Slotting
content: Assigning products to storage locations, usually based on how fast they move.

section_title: Stock take
content: A full physical count of all inventory in a warehouse.

section_title: Tare weight
content: The weight of an empty container, vehicle or packaging.

section_title: Gross weight
content: The total weight of the goods plus their packaging.

section_title: Net weight
content: The weight of the goods alone, without packaging.

section_title: Transshipment
content: Moving cargo from one vehicle or vessel to another on the way to its destination.

section_title: Unit load
content: Goods combined into one handling unit, such as a palletised load or a shrink-wrapped stack.

section_title: Volumetric weight
content: A weight calculated from the size of a shipment. It applies when a shipment is bulky but light.

section_title: Warehouse Management System (WMS)
content: Software that tracks stock locations, movements and orders inside a warehouse.

section_title: Zone
content: A defined area of the warehouse, such as fast-moving stock or hazardous storage.

section_title: Cold chain
content: A chain of temperature-controlled storage and transport that keeps goods within the required range.

section_title: Temperature log
content: A record of temperature readings for goods in storage or in transit.

section_title: Hazmat
content: Short for hazardous materials: goods that can pose a risk to people, property or the environment.

section_title: UN number
content: A four-digit code that identifies a dangerous good for transport.

section_title: Fragile mark
content: A label that tells handlers the carton contains breakable goods.

section_title: Pilferage
content: Theft of small quantities of goods from a shipment or warehouse.

section_title: Customs clearance
content: The process by which customs releases goods after declarations are filed and duties are settled.

section_title: Lead time
content: The time between placing an order and receiving the goods.

section_title: Expiry date
content: The date after which a product should no longer be used or sold.

section_title: Shelf life
content: How long a product stays fit for use or sale.

section_title: Serial number
content: A unique number given to an individual item, used for tracking and warranty.

section_title: Batch
content: A group of items produced together under the same conditions.

section_title: Backorder
content: An order that cannot be filled from current stock and waits for replenishment.

section_title: Consolidation
content: Combining several small shipments into one larger load to reduce cost.

section_title: Receiving dock check
content: Every inbound vehicle is checked at the dock against the ASN before unloading. Seals are verified and noted on the receiving record.

section_title: Put-away after receiving
content: After receiving, goods are moved to their bin, and the bin location is scanned into the WMS.

section_title: Daily cycle counting
content: A small set of bins is counted every day on a rotating schedule, so differences are found early without stopping operations.

section_title: Monthly stock reconciliation
content: System stock is compared with physical counts each month. Differences are investigated before any adjustment is posted.

section_title: Quarantine handling
content: Damaged or unverified goods go to a separate quarantine area and are not picked until the Warehouse Manager releases them.

section_title: Returns receiving
content: Returned goods are inspected and recorded with their return reason. They are then restocked, repaired or moved to quarantine.

section_title: Cross-docking at the dock
content: Goods that already have a dispatch order move from the dock straight to the outbound bay, with little or no storage.

section_title: Loading sequence
content: Cartons are loaded in reverse delivery order, so the first delivery is accessible when the vehicle is opened.

section_title: Load securing before departure
content: Cargo is strapped or blocked before the vehicle leaves, and the securing is checked at the gate.

section_title: Pallet build standard
content: Pallets are built square, with heavy items at the bottom and the stack kept within the height and weight limits of the goods.

section_title: Stacking limits
content: The printed stacking limit on each carton is respected. Cartons are never stacked on top of fragile goods.

section_title: Forklift safety
content: Only trained operators use forklifts. Pedestrians stay out of marked lanes, and loads are kept low while travelling.

section_title: Personal protective equipment
content: Staff wear safety shoes and gloves on the dock, and high-visibility vests in the yard.

section_title: Fire exits and extinguishers
content: Fire exits and extinguisher points are kept clear at all times. Blocked exits are reported to the Warehouse Manager at once.

section_title: Housekeeping
content: Aisles are cleared at the end of each shift, and spilled liquids are cleaned up immediately to prevent slips.

section_title: Pest control
content: Regular inspection and treatment reduce rodent and insect risk. Records are kept, especially for food and grain stock.

section_title: Cold room temperature logging
content: Temperatures in the cold area are logged at set intervals. Any reading outside the required range is escalated at once.

section_title: Dock door scheduling
content: Inbound and outbound vehicles are assigned dock doors so that loading and unloading do not overlap.

section_title: Gate check-in
content: Every vehicle is logged at the gate with its number and driver details. Gate passes are issued where needed.

section_title: Vehicle inspection before loading
content: The loading bay checks the vehicle for cleanliness, damage and fitness to carry the goods before loading starts.

section_title: Seal verification
content: Seal numbers are checked against the documents at loading and at receiving. A broken or mismatched seal is reported at once.

section_title: Container stuffing record
content: Each container load is recorded with its seal number, weight and carton count, and photographed where required.

section_title: Labelling at packing
content: Each carton gets a label with the LR number, carton number and destination before it leaves the packing station.

section_title: Barcode scanning at pick and dispatch
content: Every carton and pallet is scanned at pick, pack and dispatch, so the system matches what was actually moved.

section_title: Serial number capture
content: Serialised products are scanned at receiving and dispatch, so each unit can be traced.

section_title: Batch capture at receiving
content: Batch and expiry details are captured at receiving and linked to each bin, so that recalls can be traced.

section_title: Near-expiry monitoring
content: A weekly report lists stock close to expiry, so it can be dispatched or flagged before it becomes dead stock.

section_title: Dead stock review
content: Items that have not moved for a long time are reviewed with the client to decide on return, discount or disposal.

section_title: Safety stock settings
content: Each client's safety stock level is set in the WMS. The Warehouse Manager is alerted when stock falls below it.

section_title: Replenishment from reserve
content: Forward pick bins are topped up from reserve storage before they run out, so pickers are not held up.

section_title: Slotting by movement speed
content: Fast-moving products are placed near the dispatch bays and slow movers further back, to reduce travel time.

section_title: Order consolidation
content: Orders for the same consignee or route are combined where possible, to reduce the number of vehicles and cartons.

section_title: Packing material control
content: Cartons, tape and dunnage are issued against orders, and stock is counted monthly to control wastage.

section_title: Damage recording
content: Damage found during handling is photographed and recorded in the WMS with a damage code. The Warehouse Manager is informed.

section_title: Weighing and dimension capture
content: Each carton's weight and dimensions are recorded at packing. This supports billing and the chargeable weight calculation.

section_title: Shrinkage investigation
content: Unexplained shortages are investigated by comparing scan logs, CCTV footage where available, and count records.

section_title: Shift handover
content: Each shift ends with a handover note covering open exceptions, pending dispatches and any hazards.

section_title: Incident reporting
content: Accidents, near misses and spills are reported on the same day, with the time, location and people involved.

section_title: Access control
content: Only authorised staff and visitors enter the storage area. Visitors sign in and wear visitor badges.

section_title: Hazmat segregation
content: Hazardous goods are stored only in Zone H, and incompatible materials are kept apart as set in the storage plan.

section_title: Spill kits
content: Spill kits are placed near chemical and liquid storage, and staff are trained to use them.

section_title: Monsoon preparation
content: Before the monsoon, roofs, drains and low-lying areas are checked, and stock is moved off the floor where water can reach it.

section_title: Festival season planning
content: Peak periods before festivals are planned in advance, with extra staff, dock slots and safety stock.

section_title: Dispatch confirmation
content: A dispatch is confirmed only after the documents, weights and carton counts match the order, and the status is updated.

section_title: Pick accuracy checks
content: Random picks are re-checked each day, and any pick error is traced to the picker and the bin label.

section_title: Two-person check for high-value goods
content: High-value consignments are counted and sealed by two people, and the sealing is recorded.

section_title: Booking cancellation
content: To cancel a booking, contact the Logistics Coordinator in writing. Cancellation terms are set out in the client agreement. A booking that has already been picked up is handled as a return or re-routing request.

section_title: Pickup rescheduling
content: The sender can reschedule a pickup through the Logistics Coordinator. The new date is confirmed before the carrier is reassigned.

section_title: Failed pickup
content: If the sender is not ready at the pickup time, the attempt is logged as Pickup Attempted and a new pickup is scheduled.

section_title: Weight and volume disputes
content: If the weighed weight differs from the booked weight, the Logistics Coordinator reviews the weighment slip and the packing list before the bill is finalised.

section_title: Invoice queries
content: Billing queries must be raised in writing with the invoice number. Disputes not resolved at Level 1 move to the Operations Manager (see PO-004).

section_title: Payment terms
content: Payment terms are set in the client agreement. Check the agreement, or contact your account manager, for the terms that apply to you.

section_title: Extended cover at booking
content: Extended insurance cover must be selected at booking. Goods without extended cover are protected only up to the carrier liability limit (see PO-001).

section_title: Prohibited and restricted goods
content: Goods that are illegal to transport, or that the carrier does not accept, cannot be booked. Ask the Logistics Coordinator before booking any unusual item.

section_title: Hazardous goods rules
content: Hazardous goods move only with a carrier holding a valid hazmat certificate, and they are stored only in Zone H (see SP-002 and WO-002).

section_title: Customs and declarations
content: The client is responsible for the accuracy of invoices, HS codes and declared values on export and import documents.

section_title: Force majeure
content: Delays caused by events outside FleetHarbor's control, such as natural disasters, strikes or government action, are not treated as service failures. The status and reason code are updated as events happen.

section_title: Holiday schedule
content: Deliveries run Monday to Saturday between 9:00 AM and 7:00 PM. Public holidays can change the schedule, and the Logistics Coordinator confirms revised dates.

section_title: Complaint handling
content: Complaints start with the Logistics Coordinator for the lane. Unresolved complaints move to the Operations Manager and then to the Head of Operations (see PO-004).

section_title: Consignee refusal
content: If the consignee refuses delivery, the shipment is logged as a Failed Attempt with the refusal reason, and the sender is contacted for the next step.

section_title: Data access requests
content: Clients can request records of their own shipments through the Logistics Coordinator. Consignee data is handled as described in the data and privacy policy (see PO-003).

section_title: Document retention
content: Shipping documents are kept in the system for the period set in the client agreement and as required by applicable law.

section_title: Packaging responsibility
content: The client is responsible for packaging that suits the goods and the route. FleetHarbor may refuse packaging that appears unsafe and will record the reason.

section_title: Client portal access
content: Each client user has a named login for the client portal. Access should be shared only with users the client has authorised.

section_title: Contact changes
content: The client must tell FleetHarbor in writing when a pickup or consignee contact changes, so that the updated details are used for dispatch and delivery.

section_title: Escalation of priority shipments
content: A priority shipment moves to the next escalation level if it has no resolution within 4 hours (see PO-004 and CO-002).

section_title: Support hours
content: Support is provided through the Logistics Coordinator during working hours. Priority issues follow the escalation matrix.

section_title: How do I know my order has shipped?
content: Check the tracking page with your order ID or LR number. The status changes to In Transit once the carrier has picked up the shipment (see SS-002).

section_title: Can I ask for a different delivery time?
content: Deliveries run from 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Ask the Logistics Coordinator for your lane to request a time within these hours. Any delivery outside them needs written approval from the Operations Manager and the client.

section_title: What is an LR number?
content: The LR number is the lorry receipt number generated at booking. It is shared with the carrier, so use it to track the shipment after booking (see TM-001).

section_title: Why does my order show On Hold?
content: A hold means an exception was logged with a reason code, such as missing documents, weather or capacity limits. The order is not cancelled, and the reason code is shown on the tracking page.

section_title: Can I change my order after it is dispatched?
content: After dispatch, changes must be requested through the carrier, and a re-routing fee may apply. Ask the Logistics Coordinator for your lane as soon as possible.

section_title: How many delivery attempts will be made?
content: Up to three delivery attempts are made. After the third failed attempt, the shipment returns to the origin hub (see DP-001).

section_title: Do I need to sign for my delivery?
content: Proof of delivery needs the receiver's name, a signature or OTP confirmation, and a timestamp (see DP-002).

section_title: Can I send goods without an invoice?
content: No. Dispatch is blocked in the system until the mandatory documents, including the invoice and packing list, are attached (see SP-003).

section_title: Do you deliver on Sundays?
content: Standard deliveries run Monday to Saturday. Any Sunday or out-of-hours delivery needs written approval from the Operations Manager and the client (see DP-003).

section_title: Why was my shipment returned?
content: A shipment is returned after three failed delivery attempts, or when a return is agreed. Its status then changes to Returned (see SS-005).

section_title: How long do I have to return goods?
content: Returns are accepted within 10 days of delivery for unused goods in their original packaging (see PO-002).

section_title: Who pays for return freight?
content: Return freight is charged to the client unless the return results from a FleetHarbor error (see PO-002).

section_title: How much is my shipment insured for?
content: Carrier liability is limited to the declared value of the goods, unless extended cover was bought at booking (see PO-001).

section_title: Is my contact information shared with the carrier?
content: Consignee details are used only for delivery. They are removed from active systems 90 days after proof of delivery and are not shared with third parties (see PO-003).

section_title: Why is my tracking not updating?
content: In-transit shipments refresh every 30 minutes. If the status has not changed in 24 hours, contact the Logistics Coordinator for your lane (see FAQ-001 and OT-001).

section_title: What is the difference between an order ID and an LR number?
content: Order IDs begin with ORD-. LR numbers begin with LR- and are shared with the carrier, so use the LR number to track after booking (see OT-002).

section_title: How long does delivery take?
content: Standard windows are 2 to 4 business days for intra-state shipments and 4 to 7 business days for inter-state shipments (see CO-002).

section_title: How do I mark a shipment as priority?
content: Priority shipments are flagged at booking. They receive daily status checks from the Logistics Coordinator (see CO-002).

section_title: Who do I contact if my issue is not resolved?
content: Start with the Logistics Coordinator (Level 1). If the issue is still open, it goes to the Operations Manager (Level 2), then to the Head of Operations (Level 3). A priority shipment moves up after 4 hours without resolution (see PO-004).

section_title: Do you handle hazardous goods?
content: Yes, but hazardous goods move only with a carrier that holds a valid hazmat certificate, and they are stored only in Zone H (see SP-002 and WO-002).

section_title: Can you store my goods in your warehouse?
content: FleetHarbor offers warehousing from its Ahmedabad, Vadodara and Rajkot warehouses (see CO-001). Contact your account manager to arrange storage.

section_title: How are goods picked from the warehouse?
content: Perishable goods are picked FEFO, and all other goods are picked FIFO (see WO-003).

section_title: What does Failed Attempt mean on my tracking?
content: Failed Attempt means a delivery was tried but not completed. Each attempt is recorded with a reason code (see DP-001 and SS-005).

section_title: What happens if I refuse a delivery?
content: The refusal is logged as a Failed Attempt with its reason, and the sender is contacted for the next step.

section_title: How do I report missing cartons?
content: Compare the carton count with the packing list, note the shortage on the POD at delivery, and raise a claim within 7 days with photos and the invoice (see PO-001).

section_title: Is my order confirmed as soon as I place it?
content: An order moves through Order Created and then Order Confirmed. The booking is made within 2 hours of confirmation (see LW-001 and SP-001).

section_title: How do I track a shipment on the portal?
content: Log in to the client portal and enter your order ID or LR number on the tracking page. You can also call support to speak to a team member (see OT-001).

section_title: What if I cannot receive the goods at the delivery address?
content: Tell the Logistics Coordinator the best time for the next attempt. Attempts are made only within delivery hours (see DP-003).

section_title: What stages does an order go through?
content: Every order moves through six stages: Order Created, Order Confirmed, Picked, Packed, Dispatched and Delivered (see LW-001).

section_title: Does an exception cancel my order?
content: No. An exception is logged as a hold with a reason code and does not cancel the order (see LW-001).

section_title: What should I do if my tracking shows Delayed?
content: Check the reason code on the tracking page. Weather, missing documents and capacity limits are the usual reasons. Contact the Logistics Coordinator if there is no update within 24 hours (see SS-004).

section_title: Who signs the POD for a delivery?
content: The receiver signs, or confirms by OTP, and the Delivery Executive records the receiver's name and a timestamp (see DP-002).

section_title: FleetHarbor AI Global Network and Executive Overview
content: FleetHarbor AI Logistics is an international multi-modal third-party logistics (3PL) carrier with dual headquarters in Singapore and Rotterdam. Operating across 140 countries with 280 strategic facilities, FleetHarbor provides Ocean Freight (FCL/LCL), Global Air Cargo, Intermodal Road and Rail linehaul, Temperature-controlled Life Sciences cold-chain under policy CC-POL-9921, and licensed customs brokerage at over 60 global gateways.

section_title: Customer Terms of Carriage, Billing SLAs and Payment Schedules
content: FleetHarbor customer accounts operate under three credit tiers: Enterprise Corporate (Net 30/60 days with dedicated account rep), Healthcare Priority (GDP mandatory compliance, Net 45), and Standard Commercial (Net 15 days or pre-paid). Booking cancellations made before container placement incur zero fees; dispatch cancellations are subject to $150-$450 empty haulage fees.

section_title: Ocean and Air Cargo Free Time and Demurrage Fee Schedule
content: Ocean Import FCL containers receive 5 calendar days of free time following vessel discharge. Ocean Export FCL containers receive 7 calendar days before departure. Demurrage rates after free time are $85/day for Days 1-5 and $150/day thereafter for dry containers. Reefer containers incur $180/day for Days 1-3 and $320/day thereafter. Air cargo free time is 48 hours from airline arrival notice.

section_title: Freight Loss and Cargo Damage Claims Submission and Settlement SOP
content: To file a cargo claim: obvious external damage must be noted on the Proof of Delivery (POD) at delivery with formal written notice within 3 days. Concealed damage must be filed within 14 calendar days. Total loss claims must be submitted within 30 days of estimated delivery date. Submissions require the signed Waybill/BOL, original supplier invoice, damage photos, and salvage estimate. FleetHarbor resolves completed claims within 21 business days.

section_title: Warehouse Safety Protocols, Zero-Harm PPE and Material Handling Rules
content: All warehouse employees and forklift operators must wear certified steel-toe shoes (ASTM F2413 / EN ISO 20345), high-visibility class 2/3 vests, and hard hats under overhead racks. Forklift speed is strictly governed to a maximum of 8 km/h (5 mph). Daily pre-shift MHE checklists are mandatory. Maintain a 3-meter safety perimeter from moving equipment at all times.

section_title: Inbound Truck Check-in, Container Seal Verification and Put-Away SOP
content: Inbound receiving SOP: Dock supervisors must match carrier container seal numbers with shipping manifests prior to cutting seals. If a seal is broken or mismatched, doors remain closed and Security is alerted. Received cargo is scanned via master barcode, inspected for transit damage, tagged with internal License Plate Number (LPN) barcodes, and moved to storage within 45 minutes (15 minutes for cold-chain items).

section_title: Mandatory International Customs Clearance Documentation Guidelines
content: International cross-border customs clearance requires: 1) Commercial Invoice stating buyer/seller names, full product description, 6-10 digit HS code, commercial currency, Incoterms 2020 rules, and country of origin; 2) Packing List detailing itemization, dimensions, gross and net weights; 3) Transport Bill of Lading or Air Waybill; 4) Certificate of Origin when claiming preferential tariff treatment. Incomplete documents trigger customs red-channel holds.

section_title: Resolving Customs Holds, Inspections and Documentation Audits
content: When a shipment status indicates 'On Hold - Customs', action depends on the hold category: HOLD-DOC requires an amended invoice or packing list within 24 hours; HOLD-VAL requires supplier payment proof or purchase order; HOLD-PGA requires partner government agency registrations (FDA, DEFRA, etc.); HOLD-PHYS requires a physical inspection at the customs exam station attended by a licensed FleetHarbor customs runner.

section_title: Pharmaceutical Cold-Chain Policy CC-POL-9921 Operating Guidelines
content: FleetHarbor Healthcare operations operate under Policy Code CC-POL-9921 complying with WHO GDP and EU Guidelines 2013/C 343/01. Validated ranges: Cryogenic / Dry Ice (-70°C to -80°C), Deep Frozen (-20°C to -10°C), Refrigerated (+2°C to +8°C, never freeze), and Controlled Room Temperature (+15°C to +25°C). All consignments carry calibrated real-time cellular/GPS sensors logging data every 10 minutes. Any temperature breach triggers immediate quarantine and a 24-hour RCA report.

section_title: Dangerous Goods Packaging, Lithium Battery Rules and Hazmat Classes 1-9
content: Hazardous materials transport complies with IATA DGR and IMDG codes. FleetHarbor accepts Classes 2 through 9 in UN-certified packaging (e.g. 4G/4GV). Standalone lithium batteries (UN3480/UN3090) shipped by air are limited to maximum 30% State of Charge (SoC), require UN 38.3 test summaries, and must carry Cargo Aircraft Only (CAO) labels. Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods (DGD) is mandatory.
